label: MQTT to EnergyID Webhook Bridge
info:
MQTT to EnergyID incoming webhook bridge (v2, fleet scale).

Subscribes to configured MQTT topic families, auto-discovers devices from MQTT topics, registers each device against EnergyID via /hello with a deterministic claimCode, and uploads each device's buffered readings to the webhookUrl that /hello returns.

State lives in global keys:
  global.eid.registry   - { deviceId: { ...meta, claimed, headers, webhookUrl, endpoint } }
  global.eid.buffers    - { deviceId: [ {ts, el, ...}, ... ] }
  global.eid.hosts      - { host: { ok, throttled, pausedUntil, ... } }

Endpoints: /hello decides where a device uploads. A Service Bus URL (servicebus.windows.net) has no request limit worth worrying about. https://hooks.energyid.eu/webhook-in is limited to 30 requests per 15 min per caller IP, shared by every device behind this bridge; the registry summary flags a fleet on /webhook-in. Devices pick up a new endpoint by themselves at their next credential refresh (EID_CREDENTIAL_REFRESH_S).

How uploads scale:
  - one request carries up to EID_MAX_BATCH_SIZE points (and EID_MAX_BATCH_BYTES of JSON) of one device;
  - readings closer than EID_MIN_POINT_SPACING_S are merged (latest value per key wins) before upload;
  - due devices are served longest-waiting first, at most EID_MAX_SENDS_PER_TICK per 10 s tick and EID_MAX_INFLIGHT at once;
  - HTTP 429/503 pauses the whole host (Retry-After honoured, doubling up to EID_HOST_PAUSE_MAX_S), not just one device;
  - 400/413/422 halve the batch until the refused point is isolated and dropped (counted in droppedPoints), so one bad point cannot block a device;
  - 401/403/404 trigger an immediate /hello for that device.

Required environment variables:
  MQTT_BROKER_HOST=<mqtt-broker-host>
  MQTT_BROKER_PORT=8883
  MQTT_BROKER_USER=<mqtt-user>
  MQTT_BROKER_PASSWORD=<mqtt-password, use in broker credentials as ${MQTT_BROKER_PASSWORD}>
  ENERGYID_PROVISIONING_KEY=<EnergyID provisioning key>
  ENERGYID_PROVISIONING_SECRET=<EnergyID provisioning secret>

Optional environment variables (defaults):
  EID_DEVICE_ALLOWLIST=            CSV of deviceIds; empty = allow all
  EID_DEVICE_MAPPINGS_JSON=        JSON mapping override (see "Metric mapping quick guide")
  EID_MIN_POINT_SPACING_S=60       merge readings closer than this; 0 = keep every sample
  EID_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=1000          points per request (EnergyID accepts at most 1000)
  EID_MAX_BATCH_BYTES=200000       JSON bytes per request (Service Bus messages are max 256 KB)
  EID_MAX_BUFFER_POINTS=5000       per device; oldest points are dropped beyond this
  EID_MAX_INFLIGHT=                upload requests in flight at once, all devices together (empty = auto)
  EID_MAX_SENDS_PER_TICK=          new upload requests per 10 s tick (empty = auto: twice what the claimed fleet
                                   needs at its upload intervals, min 8)
  EID_BACKLOG_INTERVAL_S=60        a device with more buffered points than one batch is due again after this
  EID_HOST_PAUSE_MAX_S=900         longest pause of a host after repeated 429/503
  EID_HELLO_PER_TICK=              /hello calls per 5 s tick (empty = auto: 2..10, clears the due list in ~5 min)
  EID_HELLO_COOLDOWN_S=300         min seconds between /hello calls for one device
  EID_HELLO_IDLE_AFTER=12          after this many /hello calls without a claim, a device slows down to
  EID_HELLO_IDLE_COOLDOWN_S=1800   this cadence (keep it under 3600: EnergyID drops a registration request after 60 min)
  EID_CREDENTIAL_REFRESH_S=86400   claimed devices re-run /hello after this (and 6 h before their token expires)
  EID_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_S=120       a batch without response for this long is put back in the buffer
  EID_HTTP_TIMEOUT_S=30            timeout of the /hello and upload requests
EID_BATCH_INTERVAL_S from v1 is gone: the upload interval comes from the device's EnergyID upload policy.

Throughput: requests per hour needed ~= claimed devices x 3600 / uploadInterval (900 s policy: 4 per device per hour). The caps follow the fleet size automatically; set them only to throttle the bridge on purpose.

Import note: the broker host and port use ${MQTT_BROKER_HOST} and ${MQTT_BROKER_PORT}. MQTT credentials are intentionally not exported; set the broker username/password after import, or use ${MQTT_BROKER_USER} and ${MQTT_BROKER_PASSWORD} in the broker credentials fields. Prefer global/process environment variables for real secrets, not flow-level values in JSON that may be shared later.

Upgrading from v1: import over the existing tab (same node ids) and keep your own "Route + extract + register + buffer" node if you customised it; v2 does not change it. The registry and buffers are kept.

Diagnostics: click "Show registry summary". payload.problems lists, one line per device or host, anything that needs a look. payload.endpoints counts claimed devices per endpoint, payload.minutesSinceLastUpload gives p50/p95/max over claimed devices, payload.hosts shows throttling per host.
Claiming: an unclaimed device gets a claim code from /hello and stays claimable in EnergyID while the bridge keeps saying hello. Once claimed, the next /hello returns the webhook credentials and uploads start.

Metric mapping quick guide
info:
Metric mapping quick guide

Edit EID_DEVICE_MAPPINGS_JSON on the tab to choose what gets sent. Leave empty to use defaults.

Example:
[{"topic":"tele/+/SENSOR","deviceId":"tasmota-${1}","deviceName":"Tasmota ${1}","deviceType":"tasmota","channels":[{"key":"el","path":"ENERGY.Total","scale":1},{"key":"pwr","path":"ENERGY.Power","scale":0.001}]}]

Standard EnergyID keys: el, el-i, pwr, pwr-i, gas, pv, wind, chp, dh, dc, solar, ev, bat, bat-i, heat, dw.

Use Show unmapped topics to find new MQTT topics or payloads that do not match a mapping.
